bug_description.normalized: During subsetting of an attacker-supplied font, `_gsub_closure` reaches `OT::SingleSubstFormat1::closure` and creates a stack `Coverage::Iter` for the font's GSUB coverage table. The iterator object is not fully cleared before its format-specific fields are initialized, so `iter.get_glyph()` propagates stack-uninitialized state into `glyph_id`. `hb_set_t::has(glyph_id)` stores that poisoned value into `page_map_t key` in `hb_set_t::page_for`, and `hb_vector_t::bfind()` consumes it in the binary-search comparison branch where MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value. A later upstream fix zeroed the iterator object before selecting the active union member.

source.description: Creates the stack-local `Coverage::Iter` that will walk the attacker-controlled GSUB Coverage table. MSan's origin report names this local `iter` allocation in `SingleSubstFormat1::closure` as the source of the uninitialized value.
source.value_from: Coverage table contents inside the fuzzed font's GSUB SingleSubstFormat1 subtable, reached during `hb_subset(..., drop_ot_layout=false)`.

sink.description: The binary-search comparison consumes `x.major`, which was derived from the uninitialized glyph id. MSan reports the resulting control-flow use at line 214 in `bfind()`.

root_cause.description: The iterator initialization logic selects a format-specific union arm but does not first clear the whole `Coverage::Iter` object. The later upstream fix added a full-object zeroing step before this format dispatch, matching MSan's report that the uninitialized value originates from the stack `iter` object.

parser_admitted.description: When `drop_ot_layout` is false, subsetting explicitly enters GSUB closure by calling `_gsub_closure(face, initial_gids_to_retain)` on the attacker-supplied face.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSan reports that the uninitialized value was created by the stack allocation of `iter` in this closure frame.

coarse_trace.summary: The subset planner enters GSUB closure on the attacker-controlled face and calls `hb_ot_layout_lookups_substitute_closure` with a non-empty glyph-retention set.

A stack `Coverage::Iter` is created for the font's GSUB Coverage table, but its initialization leaves iterator state uninitialized; `iter.get_glyph()` yields a poisoned glyph id that is passed into `c->glyphs->has()`.

The uninitialized glyph id is converted into a `page_map_t key` and sent into `page_map.bsearch()`, where `hb_vector_t::bfind()` uses the poisoned key in its binary-search comparison and MSan reports use-of-uninitialized-value.

fine_trace.note: Creates the stack-local iterator over the attacker-controlled Coverage table in the fuzzed GSUB subtable. MSan's origin record identifies this closure frame's local `iter` object as the allocation where the uninitialized value begins.

Initialization reads the Coverage format and initializes only the selected union arm (`u.format1` or `u.format2`). The iterator object is not fully cleared first, so stack bytes in `iter` remain indeterminate; the later upstream fix added a full-object zeroing step before this block.

The closure extracts a glyph id from the partially initialized iterator. MSan's stack-origin report ties the uninitialized value to `iter`, and this `glyph_id` is the first value pulled from that iterator and then forwarded down the crashing path.

The glyph id is passed into the retained-glyph set lookup. `_populate_gids_to_retain` already seeded this set with glyph 0 before GSUB closure, so `has()` performs a real `page_for(glyph_id)` lookup on a populated `hb_set_t`.

The set lookup stores the uninitialized glyph id into the search key by computing `get_major(g)`. MSan's stack trace explicitly reports this line as where the uninitialized value was stored to memory before the final comparison.
The poisoned `key.major` is forwarded unchanged into the page-map binary search that resolves membership in the glyph-retention set.

The binary search compares `x.major` from the local key against `arrayZ[mid].major`. Because `x.major` came from the uninitialized iterator path, the comparison result `c` is tainted and MSan reports use-of-uninitialized-value at the subsequent branch on line 214 (`else if (c > 0)`).

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` and sample metadata `fixed_commit` are unrelated build-system changes and do not address this MSan iterator-initialization bug. The source-history fix that matches the saved sanitizer evidence is the later upstream change that zeroes `Coverage::Iter` before format dispatch.

format.name: OpenType font
format.contract: A font blob that loads as an `hb_face_t` and, during `hb_subset(..., drop_ot_layout=false)`, reaches `_gsub_closure` and then `OT::SingleSubstFormat1::closure` for at least one GSUB lookup so the `Coverage::Iter` loop executes and calls `c->glyphs->has(iter.get_glyph())`.
